documents.text:
===== PAGE 1 =====
This is sample data provided for OPL No: OPL-GA-1201A-01
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL)
CALIBER purposes only Sheet 1 of 1
OPL Title Mechanical Seal Flush (API Plan 11) Verification Discipline Mechanical
Equipment GA-1201A - HEXANE FEED PUMP Area / Unit 1200 - HEXANE FEED SYSTEM
Related Interlock SEQ-1201 (SIL 1) P&ID; Ref TJC-LLD-PID-1201
Classification: [ ] Basic Knowledge [ ] Improvement [X] Trouble Case Aspect: P-Q-C-D-S-M-E
1. PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE
This One Point Lesson explains mechanical seal flush (api plan 11) verification for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP) in
the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM. Confirm seal flush dP > 1.5 bar before start. Low flush = seal face overheating and hexane
leak to atmosphere. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so
the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
2. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Hazard note: this equipment is HIGH CRITICAL handling n-Hexane at up to 16 barg / 80 degC. Observe the following before
and during the task:
nApply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
nIsolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
nWear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
nBeware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
nUse certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.
3. TOOLS & MATERIALS REQUIRED
lStandard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
lLOTO padlocks and permit
lLaser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
lFeeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
lCorrect spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
lLifting gear and slings (certified)
4. DETAILED PROCEDURE / STEPS
Step Action Check / Acceptance
1 Line up discharge flush to seal chamber and open flush isolation Isolation & LOTO verified
2 Check PDI-1201 reads 1.5-2.5 bar dP across the flush orifice RO-1201 Parts match BOM / spec
3 Verify no visible leak or drip at the gland / seal drain Torque / clearance to spec
4 If dP low, isolate and inspect orifice RO-1201 for plugging by polymer/dirt No leak / smooth operation
5 Confirm quench (Plan 62) N2/steam is lined up to the outboard side Record in equipment history
5. COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING
Symptom Likely Cause Action
Hexane leak observed at GA-1201A API Plan 11 flush orifice RO-1201 partially Replaced JC T2100 mechanical seal cartridge,
seal gland during operation, seal dr. plugged causing seal face. cleaned flush orifice, v.
GA-1201A tripped on VSHH-1201 high Angular misalignment 0.12 mm/100mm after Laser re-aligned pump/motor, re-shimmed
vibration 7.4 mm/s foundation settlement motor feet, vibration back to.
Bearing DE noisy with rising Outer race spalling on DE bearing due to Renewed DE bearing 7310 BECBM, flushed
temperature TI-1201 trend prolonged misalignment housing, refilled ISO VG 68
6. KEY LEARNING POINTS
nConfirm seal flush dP > 1.5 bar before start. Low flush = seal face overheating and hexane leak to atmosphere.
nRespect the interlock SEQ-1201: e.g. PSLL-1201 trips at < 0.5 barg - never defeat it without a permit.
nAlways cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID; TJC-LLD-PID-1201 before working on GA-1201A.
nRecord the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
Prepared by Reviewed by (Supervisor) Approved by (Manager) Date of Sharing
Panel Operator / Technician Wahyu Setiadi (EMP-1113) Arya Wibisono (EMP-0912) Sunday, 22 March 2026
Cross-ref tag GA-1201A across Datasheet, GA, P&ID, Interlock and Maintenance History.

premature bearing/seal failure. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step
method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

lLOTO padlocks and permit
lLaser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
lFeeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
lCorrect spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
lLifting gear and slings (certified)
4. DETAILED PROCEDURE / STEPS
Step Action Check / Acceptance
1 Isolate and LOTO the motor, remove coupling guard Isolation & LOTO verified
2 Mount laser alignment brackets across the coupling spacer Parts match BOM / spec
3 Rotate 0-90-180-270 deg and capture readings Torque / clearance to spec
4 Target angular < 0.05 mm/100 mm and offset < 0.05 mm No leak / smooth operation

protects the pump from deadhead overheating. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the

lCorrect PPE for the fluid handled

Step Action Check / Acceptance

2 Watch that FIC-1201 stays above the 9 m3/h minimum continuous flow Parameter within limit

1. PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE
This One Point Lesson explains cold alignment vs hot check for hexane service for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP) in
the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM. Hexane at operating temperature grows the casing; a good cold alignment must include the
correct thermal-growth offset. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step
method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
2. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Hazard note: this equipment is HIGH CRITICAL handling n-Hexane at up to 16 barg / 80 degC. Observe the following before
and during the task:
nApply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
nIsolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.

nBeware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
nUse certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.
3. TOOLS & MATERIALS REQUIRED
lStandard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
lLOTO padlocks and permit
lLaser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
lFeeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
lCorrect spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
lLifting gear and slings (certified)
4. DETAILED PROCEDURE / STEPS
Step Action Check / Acceptance
1 Take cold alignment with the specified target offsets applied Isolation & LOTO verified
2 After ~2 h at temperature, do a hot-check on the coupling Parts match BOM / spec
3 Compare hot readings against the cold targets Torque / clearance to spec
4 Adjust thermal-growth compensation if repeat vibration trips occur No leak / smooth operation
5 Log both cold and hot data in the machine history file Record in equipment history

1. PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE
This One Point Lesson explains vibration trend monitoring & alarm response (vshh-1201) for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED
PUMP) in the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM. A rising vibration trend predicts bearing failure days in advance and lets you plan a
repair before a trip. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so
the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
2. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Hazard note: this equipment is HIGH CRITICAL handling n-Hexane at up to 16 barg / 80 degC. Observe the following before
and during the task:
nDe-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
nInform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
nTake care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
nVerify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
nWear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.
3. TOOLS & MATERIALS REQUIRED
lHART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
lLoop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
lDigital multimeter and clamp meter
lSpan/zero test gas or reference standards
lTorque screwdriver and small hand tools
lCertified test/inhibit permit
4. DETAILED PROCEDURE / STEPS
Step Action Check / Acceptance
1 Record VT-1201 on the daily PdM route in mm/s RMS Loop isolated / under permit
2 Note alarm at 4.5 mm/s and trip at 7.1 mm/s (VSHH-1201) Reference standard traceable
3 A rise greater than 1 mm/s within a week = plan a bearing inspection As-found & as-left recorded
4 Correlate the vibration rise with TI-1201 bearing temperature Trip / control action verified
5 Escalate to reliability engineer if the 1x running-speed component dominates Return to service confirmed
5. COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING
Symptom Likely Cause Action
Scheduled proof test of low-low suction Switch set-point drift found +0.08 barg during Recalibrated PSLL-1201 to 0.5 barg trip,
pressure trip proof test function tested to DCS
PDI-1201 reading erratic, seal-flush low Impulse lines fouled with hexane Cleaned impulse lines and re-zeroed PDI-1201
alarm nuisance-tripping residue/polymer fines transmitter
Discharge flow control hunting, Loop poorly tuned after transmitter re-range Re-ranged FT-1201 and retuned FIC-1201 PID
FIC-1201 oscillating parameters
6. KEY LEARNING POINTS
nA rising vibration trend predicts bearing failure days in advance and lets you plan a repair before a trip.
nRespect the interlock SEQ-1201: e.g. PSLL-1201 trips at < 0.5 barg - never defeat it without a permit.
nAlways cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID; TJC-LLD-PID-1201 before working on GA-1201A.
